changes: NOTHING WAS CHANGED. This is not a transcription: the manufacturer serves this model as a text file, so it was frozen byte-for-byte under vendor/ and the whole file - model text and the vendor's own comment blocks - was appended below a header of our own. No parameter was removed (unlike models/jfet/lsk489.lib and models/bjt_pnp/ls350.lib, where mfg= had to be stripped because ngspice evaluates it as an expression and dies; this file has no mfg=), no value was rounded, reordered or 'corrected', and the model NAME was left exactly as served. Verifiable rather than asserted: diff <(grep -v '^\*' <vendor file>) <(grep -v '^\*' <this file>) is empty. One consequence worth knowing: the vendor file uses CRLF and our header uses LF, so the assembled file has MIXED line endings. That is deliberate - normalising the whole file rewrites the vendor bytes and breaks the diff above, silently. It happened once during L25 and only the diff caught it.
reason: T7 (ADR-016), NC-017. Two of these form the negative-rail bias reference of the gain block (circuits/preamp/gain_block.py:252-253, footprint FP_DO35); it is the only diode in the signal-path bias chain and ADR-016 listed it as 'mai verificato'. THE PART WAS NOT SUBSTITUTED, IT WAS ATTRIBUTED: 1N4148 is a generic industry type number, so T7 is satisfied by naming the manufacturer whose model and lifecycle statement the project stands on. onsemi publishes both - six OPN, all Active, read from the product page's own JSON-LD - while Vishay serves a newer datasheet but no SPICE model to a non-browser client.
notes: THREE NAMES, ALL CORRECT, AND THE FILE THAT LOOKS RIGHT IS THE WRONG ONE. The part is the 1N4148; the vendor file is called 1n914.lib; the model inside is called D1N914. onsemi files the 1N4148 under the 1N914 document - its 1N4148 product page links exactly one datasheet, 1n914-d.pdf - and the model file's own header says 'Product: 1N/FDLL914/A/B / 916/A/B / 4148 / 4448, Package: DO-35 / LL-34'. Meanwhile /download/models/lib/1n4148.lib returns HTTP 200 and a REAL 1189-byte file containing .SUBCKT 1N4148WT - the SOD-323 variant, not the DO-35 this project uses - which ngspice would load without a word. That is docs/limitations.md #20. This file is named for the PART, because that is what circuits/ instantiates; the model name inside is the vendor's and was not touched. Do not 'correct' either. CROSS-CHECK (datasheet 1N914/D, September 2024 Rev. 6, the 1N4148 row and not the 914B row), ngspice 47, set temp = 25: V_F 0.766187 V at IF = 10 mA against a 1.0 V MAXIMUM (INSIDE, 23% margin); C_T 0.8687 pF at VR = 0, 1 MHz against a 4.0 pF MAXIMUM (INSIDE). BOTH PUBLISHED LIMITS INSIDE, and both reproduce L24 to the digit. Worth knowing rather than comforting: C_T sits 4.6x below the guaranteed ceiling, so the model describes a typical or better specimen, not the worst case the datasheet permits - immaterial for a bias diode at 1 mA, material in a signal path. At the actual working point the model gives V_F = 0.631952 V at 1 mA, where the datasheet specifies nothing. A LIVE INSTANCE OF docs/limitations.md #19 SITS IN THIS DATASHEET: the reverse-current row at VR = 20 V, TA = 150 C extracts as '50 mA' and reads 50 uA on the rendered page - wrong by 1000x, silently. Neither locked limit is affected. NO KF/AF, therefore NO 1/f noise - in this repo only models/jfet/lsk489.lib has flicker noise, which is why NC-004 does not close when the real models arrive. Any noise figure computed with this device is a floor without flicker and must say so next to the number.
